To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the specimen with the best results is the one which presents a higher value of damage and also, it is the specimen that presents a higher value for damage distribution in a smaller area.
we have found the most appropriate specimen geometry to be used for the forging process, in terms of the location of the fracture.

The specimen with the highest critical damage value is the one with a 45° angle between the specimen and the compression direction, and the specimen with the highest probability of crack appearance is the one with 30° angle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of different specimen geometrical shapes in order to find the most appropriate shape for the study of the damage evolution in the material during a forging process.
the study of different geometries for the compression tests in order to determine the most suitable one for the simulation of forging processes.
the design of the geometry of specimens for compression tests so that the crack location can be predicted by numerical methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the specimen geometry which shows the best performance in the compression test between plane shape dies is the one which shows a crack in the most critical area, i.e., the one which shows the most severe damage value in this zone.
the best geometry for the appearance of cracks is the one with the highest aspect ratio (length/diameter) which is the specimen with the lowest diameter.

the best design of specimen to study the damage by forging is the one which has the highest value for the damage variable at its centre, which is the most likely place to appear the crack, and which has the most homogeneous distribution of damage in its volume.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the specimen geometry that best suits our purposes would be the specimen with a notch in its middle, which would be a good candidate for future experiments.
the best specimen geometry for the forging process to be simulated is the one with the largest damage value in the center of its cross section.

the most critical damage is attained in the specimen with the smallest section, but the most critical damage distribution is obtained in a specimen with a larger section, which would allow the prediction of the place where a crack is likely to appear in a forging process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the specimen with the best damage distribution and, therefore, the best location for the crack to be generated, is the cylindrical specimen with a 1.5 mm radius and a height of 10 mm.

the damage attained in the specimens with the highest values of the damage parameter (i.e. the most likely place to appear cracks) are those which have been forged with a lower value of the reduction ratio.
the specimen geometry has a significant influence on the damage distribution in the material and therefore on the location of the crack.
